html:
The Gambia Colony and Protectorate was the British territory along the lower Gambia River in West Africa, the narrow strip that became The Gambia. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Britain founded Bathurst, today's Banjul, on an island at the river mouth in 1816, as a base against the slave trade after its ban. Groundnuts became the main export. Up the river, Mandinka kingdoms, heirs of Kaabu and the Mali Empire, were torn for decades by wars between Muslim reformers and older ruling families.

The French held the land all around, in Senegal. In 1889 the two powers fixed the border at roughly ten kilometres on each side of the river, which is why the country is so thin. Britain declared a protectorate over the interior in 1894. The Gambia became independent in 1965.
